Read-only; nothing written, no checks run, no subagents.
## FINDINGS
**F1. Listed blocks do not start with their title line — 5 blocks** (check (c), §90.2.3)

- File `rows`/`structure`; ids `b_KZEEK23PGE` ("Hearing Impairment", ent), `b_XHY6T9JDVT` ("Strabismus", ent), `b_QVGNGTAFZY` ("Dehydration", GI), `b_XG077GNK6X` ("Immunization Guidelines", neuro), `b_XCV0FB06EM` ("Bleeding Disorders", hematology).

- Evidence (peds-dump.txt): each block's first paragraph(s) are blank; the T-marked title line sits later — para 1 in the first four blocks, **para 30** in b_XG077GNK6X (30 blank paragraphs precede "Immunization Guidelines").
- Rule: §90.2.3 — "listed with its title line's text exactly when it **starts with a title line**", plus the brief's check (c) ("not after blank paragraphs or an image").

- Correction: split each block at its title line. The leading blank paragraphs remain a separate blank block taking the preceding item's section (Leader ruling seq 666 (1)); the note block then genuinely starts with its title line and the `listed` entry stands. For b_XG077GNK6X the split point is paragraph 30.
**F2. Missing split — `b_XHY6T9JDVT` (Strabismus) holds two titled notes** (§90.2.3)

- The block's para 8 "Patch exercises" is a title line (T-marked, ≤80 chars, followed by content para 9 "If untreated after age 2, amblyopia results"). §90.2.3: a prose block holding several notes, each starting with its own title line, is split so each titled note is its own block. The drafts' only split is hematology b_XD0Z19TEP9.
- Correction: split at paragraph 8; the new block is listed "Patch exercises" → eye-disorders (it is the strabismus-treatment note).
**F3. `general-files-peds.json` labs order violates §30.2 table order** (check (b))

- Draft labs order: Bacterial Pathogens, EBV serology, ABG Worksheet – Cases, ABG Workshop Workbook, Clinical Lab & Transfusion Reference, Urinalysis & Culture, Urinalysis & Culture 2026 – Summary, PANCE Histology — as-is files first.

- Rule: §90.3.1 "fixed placements come first, then the others in 30 §30.2 table order" — §30.2's Word-documents table precedes its files table. The committed, already-reviewed fm and em drafts (tools/curate/general-files.json) both use: ABG Worksheet (d_5K8ARJRYFN), ABG Workshop (d_W5CH6PSWEG), Clinical Lab (d_6CC54CR960), Urinalysis & Culture (d_9T1BK0WDG3), Bacterial Pathogens (d_77CRGHXNDK), EBV serology (d_ET2PJXFNTB), Urinalysis 2026 Summary (d_W0DJ0C3768), PANCE Histology (d_37E1NN0SQA).
- Correction: reorder the peds labs entries to that sequence.
**F4. Endocrinology — the hypercalcemia cluster sits under "Thyroid and parathyroid disorders" on a loose fit** (§90.2.1; "real fit, not loose")

- Ids: `r_3YTV11HMZW` (Hypercalcemia topic), and cause rows `r_VJZKRJB7A1` (Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia), `r_F3KN1NS29V` (SQ fat necrosis), `r_F7TDGMRZQK` (Williams), `r_G23BT3RK1T` (Granulomatous), `r_0A97P4N4X8` (Vitamin D intoxication), `r_4674M4QXEC` (Immobilization) — all members of `thyroid-and-parathyroid-disorders` in structure/endocrinology.json.

- Rule: §90.2.1 each topic goes to the category of its condition; fitting none → `other`; fit must be real, not loose (ruling 3; the FM precedent put the analogous cause-row group AEIOU TIPS under "Urgent Care — other"). Hypercalcemia and these causes are not thyroid/parathyroid disorders; only `r_71C0ZJXPYD` (Hyperparathyroidism) is, and FHH is a calcium-sensing/parathyroid-adjacent case.

- Correction: Hyperparathyroidism (and arguably FHH) stay; the remaining rows and the Hypercalcemia topic go to "Endocrinology — other" — or the whole cluster stays if the Leader rules the clinical-coherence position. **Both positions; needs the Leader if the curator disagrees.**
**F5. Derm exanthem rows vs a mechanical reading of Leader ruling 2** (leader point, both positions)
- Ids `r_MG35NPAKAD` (Mumps), `r_JVX9EFK8MQ` (Roseola Infantum – 6th Disease), `r_PVNBC7F28Q` (Erythema Infectiosum – 5th Disease), drafted to "Infectious disorders".

- Mechanical reading of ruling 2: Mumps, Roseola and Erythema infectiosum are listed verbatim under Infectious Diseases → "Viral infections", so they would move to a borrowed section in dermatology. The curator's position: ruling 2 borrows a category only when the home system has no real fit (its recorded applications — Teething, CNS neoplasms, Retinoblastoma, ear FB — are all no-fit cases; the same logic kept Acute rheumatic fever under "Traumatic, infectious, and inflammatory heart conditions" even though ARF is verbatim under ID Bacterial infections); here the home system's "Infectious disorders" already holds her exanthem rows ("Viral exanthems" is a listed subitem covering Roseola/EI; Mumps and Scarlet fever are the weakest fits).

- My note: the curator's placement preserves her exanthem-table grouping and matches how ruling 2 was applied elsewhere, but Mumps (and Scarlet fever) are the cases where "real fit" is thinnest. **Unsettled from the rules — Leader point if the curator disagrees.**
**F6. `general-items-peds.json` — procedures prominence label** (§90.3.1 prominent)

- Draft: `procedures: prominent: false, howto: null`, justified as "only a few procedures are tied to listed conditions". But ≥3 PAEA-listed conditions need procedures: lumbar puncture (Meningitis, Fever in the infant), reduction (Radial head subluxation), foreign-body removal (Foreign body, Cerumen impaction), reduction (Paraphimosis), air/contrast enema (Intussusception) — so `prominent: true`.
- Correction: set prominent true. Outcome unchanged either way (howto stays null — no top tab carries a procedures how-to), so this is a labeling correction, not a content one.

**F7. Unverifiable image-block assignments (verification owed, not a rule violation yet)** — Leader ruling on blank blocks requires the curator to check what an image block shows before assigning it. Two assignments rest solely on that check and I could not verify them: `b_KZYMT7PWZE` (neurology, image after Turner's table → developmental-milestones) and `b_EDW94P85S9` (GI, two images after Pyloric stenosis → neonatal-hyperbilirubinemia).
